title: Proposition 134: Male and Female Participation in School and Collegiate Sports

context.text: Placed on the ballot by citizen initiative. The Blue Book lists 14 statewide measures on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

question.text: Shall there be a change to the Colorado Revised Statutes creating new law restricting participation in all K-12 and collegiate school sports based on the participant's sex as determined by certain aspects of their biological reproductive system, and, in connection therewith, requiring a school, institution of higher education, or athletic association to designate each school or intramural athletic team or sport as male, female, or coeducational; only allowing participants to compete on the team or sport of their designated sex or to compete on a coeducational team; creating an exception to allow a female to participate on a male-designated team or sport if there is no female team available; prohibiting a government entity, licensing or accrediting organization, or athletic association from entertaining a complaint, opening an investigation, or taking other adverse action against a school for maintaining separate teams or sports for females; and providing the commissioner of education with the authority to enforce the proposed initiative for K-12 school districts?

summary.text: Requires every school-based team, sport and intramural (public, charter, private and religious schools from elementary through college) to be designated male, female or coeducational, with participants competing only on the team matching their biological sex (defined by the type of reproductive cells the body is organized to produce) or on a coeducational team; allows a female to join a male team if no female team exists; bars investigation or penalty of a school for keeping female-only teams; requires each school or district to adopt a policy; and gives the Commissioner of Education enforcement authority over K-12 districts. It does not apply to youth leagues operating separately from schools. Fiscal impact per the Blue Book: indeterminate added Department of Education workload and legal costs; minimal costs for schools and districts to update policies.

measure.yesMeans: Means that all school-based athletic teams and sports must be designated as being for biological males or biological females only, or as mixed, and requires schools and school districts to adopt policies on sex eligibility for sports.
measure.noMeans: Means that individual schools, school districts, and athletic associations may continue to set their own policies in alignment with current state and federal law about who is eligible to participate on a team or in a sport.

argumentsFor.text: Blue Book argument for: "Females should be able to compete against other females." It adds that the measure "creates a consistent, statewide standard for participation on female teams."
Blue Book argument for: "Allowing biological males to participate on female teams or in female sports jeopardizes the safety and physical and emotional boundaries of female athletes."

argumentsAgainst.text: Blue Book argument against: "The measure does not protect fairness; it turns athletic eligibility into a body inspection and manufactures new grounds for discrimination."
Blue Book argument against: "School sports should be a space where all kids can build confidence, health, and belonging and have the opportunity to learn teamwork, leadership, and goal setting."

researchNotes: Source: the official 2026 Blue Book (Legislative Council Staff, nonpartisan), which gives the ballot title, the 'what your vote means' text, an analysis with arguments for and against, and the fiscal impact. Its 'for' and 'against' arguments are the staff's own summaries of the main arguments on each side, not statements from named campaigns; the booklet points to the Secretary of State's page for supporting and opposing organizations, which was not reviewed here. Ballotpedia is cited only for the certified-measure count. Ballotpedia notes a separate road-funding initiative was certified but withdrawn after its proponents reached an agreement with the state, so it is not on the ballot.
